mariaines
May 18, 2021

I'm trying to use gh in an AWS CodeBuild project that uses an AWS CodeStar Connection to GitHub (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-CodestarConnectionSource.html)

Is this possible?

When I run gh auth login it succeeds, but then I get:

none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitHub host. To tell gh about a new GitHub host, please use `gh auth login`

Output of git remote -v looks like:

origin  https://codestar-connections.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/git-http/accountId/us-west-2/uuid/org/repo.git (fetch)
origin  https://codestar-connections.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/git-http/accountId/us-west-2/uuid/org/repo.git (push)

Trying to do: gh auth login --hostname codestar-connections.us-west-2.amazonaws.com results in a 403

Any help appreciated! (As a workaround I'm thinking of just using the REST api)

Answered by mislav May 19, 2021

I'm not familiar with AWS CodePipeline, but I do know that you cannot interact with it with GitHub CLI since it's a separate service (even though the source code of the project is technically backed by GitHub).

GitHub CLI needs the GitHub API to operate, and AWS doesn't expose the GitHub API. Therefore, specifying a domain like codestar-connections.us-west-2.amazonaws.com cannot be used for login. What would work, though, is identifying the URL that the original GitHub repository is hosted at (e.g https://github.com/owner/repo.git or https://our-github-host.org/owner/repo) and adding that as a separate git remote (e.g. git remote add upstream <url>). mislav
May 19, 2021

I'm not familiar with AWS CodePipeline, but I do know that you cannot interact with it with GitHub CLI since it's a separate service (even though the source code of the project is technically backed by GitHub).

GitHub CLI needs the GitHub API to operate, and AWS doesn't expose the GitHub API. Therefore, specifying a domain like codestar-connections.us-west-2.amazonaws.com cannot be used for login. What would work, though, is identifying the URL that the original GitHub repository is hosted at (e.g https://github.com/owner/repo.git or https://our-github-host.org/owner/repo) and adding that as a separate git remote (e.g. git remote add upstream <url>). Then, logging in to the GitHub host will enable GitHub CLI for the repo.
